newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-ROBSON LOOKS AHEAD TO CRITICAL FEW WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON LOOKS AHEAD TO CRITICAL FEW WEEKS.

text.p: Coach Bobby Robson said on Tuesday the next five weeks would prove just how good his Barcelona team really were.

On the day before Barcelona meet holders Paris St Germain in the European Cup Winners' Cup final, Robson said: "We could end up winning a treble of Spanish league, Spanish Cup and the European Cup Winners' Cup but at the same time we could end up winning nothing. The next few weeks will reveal everything."
But he refused to be drawn on his immediate future, which may well depend more on the internal politics at the Camp Nou rather than the amount of silverware Barcelona win.
Robson's future has been in considerable doubt for most of the season as his side have trailed arch-rivals Real Madrid in the title race.

"I have heard all kinds of stories that Louis van Gaal is leaving Ajax to come to Barcelona but I know nothing definite. If you want to find out what Louis van Gaal is intending to do, I suggest you talk to him."

Robson stressed he is thoroughly enjoying life in the spotlight at Barcelona and said: "I personally am not intending going anywhere. Of course this is a high pressure job but you know that when you take it, it has never been anything else."

Robson conceded Barcelona were seen as the favourites to win the Cup Winners' Cup for an unprecedented fourth time but said: "Paris St Germain have not played for 11 days while we had a very bruising match with Real Madrid on Saturday.
"That game really took a lot out of my players and I think it could have given a big advantage to the French team who are very well rested."
Although the pressure on the 64-year-old Englishman to win on Wednesday is intense, he showed he had still not lost his sense of humour.
A fight between two photographers broke out in front of him during his press conference and he said to one of them: "I could do with your aggression tomorrow. You don't fancy playing for us do you."

He said the bomb scare which delayed Barcelona's flight to Rotterdam for four hours on Monday had not unduly disturbed his squad. "They have all got over that and are just looking forward to the match."
